**Answer each of the following questions with *one sentence* including a brief explanation.**

1.  Finish the sentence with another student’s name: "If \[Name of Student\] doesn’t earn an A, then nobody should, because..." Explain your choice and your reasoning.\
    \
    If Abel Magallon doesn’t earn an A, then nobody should, because of the combination of his superb work and great attitude, which made him an excellent classmate during peer coding activities (and just generally).

    \

2.  What was the most difficult part of the class for you? List a general topic, a specific problem, a kind of work we did, etc. and explain why.\
    \
    The most challenging part of the class for me was the creative aspect of the course, as there were many opportunities to add a personal touch to assignments, which pushed me to grow the most by making the assignments more of a reflection of me.

3.  What was the easiest part of the class for you? Explain why.\
    \
    The easiest part of the course was probably the functions section, purely due to my CS and coding background, as this is typically how I write code and think.\

4.  What part of the class surprised or interested you the most? Explain why.\
    \
    The most interesting part of the class was definitely making cool plots. I am a perfectionist in my work, which is a blessing and a curse, because I typically try to do my best work for every assignment, however, there are SO many layers in R plots and tables that can be continuously added on, so it took a long time to be satisfied with my work.

5.  Give one piece of advice to a student just beginning a quarter of STAT 331 that will help them be successful in learning.\
    \
    Definitely start labs as soon as possible and do not wait until close to the due date, because, similar to writing a creative essay, being able to think about and refine your work over multiple sessions will almost guaranteed result in a better outcome.
